document_title: One Center, and the 17,210 Outside It
post_copy:
Executive Order 14426 uses the phrase artificial intelligence exactly once. That one clause carries a 180 day clock.

The clock runs out March 7th, 2027 over a queue of 661,395 pending claims in mid September. The clause asks for "a comprehensive single source". A single source is a center.

Anchorage holds 28,883 veterans on the VA's VetPop2023 model count and the three largest boroughs hold 53,796. The other 17,210 of the model's 71,006 live in a state where nearly 82 percent of communities are inaccessible by road. Census survey estimates rank Alaska first of fifty at 9.9 percent of adults.

Four sections off the Federal Register text. Nine boroughs off the VA's county model. Six shares off one Census table.

The order names no state and creates no right enforceable at law. What can a veteran in Nome walk in and ask for on March 8th, 2027?

#VetPop2023 #RuralAlaska #FederalRegister

The two veteran counts are different instruments. If anyone asks, the 9.9 percent and the rank are Census survey estimates and the 71,006 is the VA's VetPop2023 model.
The order is not an AI order. It mentions artificial intelligence once. Don't let a comment thread turn that into more than it is.

editor_notes_for_email:
SCORES 8.61 against the 7.7 threshold that applies at four-plus revision rounds. It also clears the unrelaxed 8.3. No hard fails. Round one scored 7.67 with Legibility at 5 of 10, which CLAUDE.md treats as a work order rather than a verdict, so the deck went back to Phase 8 and came back at 8.61.

THE SCORER'S ONE PRESCRIBED FIX WAS PROBED AND DECLINED, and here is the measurement. It flagged slide 04's '73,086 BACKLOG CLAIMS' at roughly 3.3 to 3.5 to 1 and said plainly it could not run a numeric probe. The probe was run on the shipped render at that string's own bounding box: glyph core rgb(142,47,28) at relative luminance 0.0787 against a plate face of rgb(205,212,215) at 0.6497, which is 5.44 to 1, above the 4.5 floor. qa.py's contrast check does not flag it either. The colour is unchanged, because changing it on a mistaken premise is the worse error.

WHAT THE REPAIR ROUNDS BOUGHT. Machine QA went from 9 fails and 150 warns to 0 fails and 3 warns, and render overflow warnings from 91 to 0. Slide 05's seven mile-ring labels went from 20px glowed type measuring 2.1 to 1 on the lit land to 24px on knockout plates. Slide 06's 14px legend, which printed MARK counts (524, 240, 115) three inches under prose giving VETERAN counts (5,239, 2,396, 1,152), is gone. The cover now carries the deck's own number. And the contact class the ledger has chased since No.55 is at zero: every additive radial pool at an object's foot is deleted from five frames and each of those frames now lays a drawn floor instead.

WHAT THEY COST, and you should know which. Slide 05's knockout plates stack into a dark ladder that hides much of the landmass they measure, so that frame is legible and less beautiful than it was. Slide 06's dot columns are now unlabelled and the shortest four are near-invisible at thumb size, so that band is honest and close to information-free. And bespoke_check's median pairwise art similarity rose from 0.343 to 0.426, because the floor is one helper shared by five frames; the fail line is 0.60 and drawn share held at 70 percent.

IF A COMMENT THREAD STARTS. The two veteran counts are different instruments and the aftercare block says so: VetPop2023 is the VA's county model, the 9.9 percent is a Census survey estimate, and the deck never divides one by the other. This is not an AI order; the phrase appears in it exactly once. One precision note to have ready: slide 03 says the VA has granted 0 waivers from minimum risk practices, where the source says minimum risk management practices required for high-impact AI use cases.

TIMING. October 8th is the first of the order's three deadlines and it is three weeks out, so this deck is at its most useful this week. Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time, and paste the first comment within 60 seconds.
